actions.action: Commit deduplication and business updates together
actions.mechanism: A unique event key and business mutation share one transaction; acknowledgement happens only after commit.
actions.implementation: Insert a partner-scoped event ID. On conflict, skip the mutation; otherwise apply it in the same transaction. Acknowledge after successful commit.
actions.check: Crash before commit and after commit but before acknowledgement; replay concurrently. Verify exactly one committed business update.
actions.risk: External side effects require separate protection; database rollback cannot undo them.

actions.mechanism: A persistent entity revision makes older or equal revisions no-ops, independently of event-ID retention.
actions.implementation: Within the deduplication transaction, conditionally update only when incoming revision exceeds stored revision. Preserve revision tombstones for deleted entities.
actions.check: Deliver revisions 12, 10, 12 under different IDs, including concurrent execution. Confirm state and revision remain at 12.
actions.risk: Revision gaps require reconciliation if payloads are incremental rather than complete state.

actions.action: Expire event records conservatively within a hard budget
actions.mechanism: First-receipt retention covers the replay window; strict expiration preserves records at the seven-day boundary.
actions.implementation: Store first receipt and expiry seven days later; never refresh duplicates. Delete only after expiry. Enforce a 2 GB dedup-storage budget, including indexes, with admission backpressure.
actions.check: Replay just before, exactly at, and after expiry; verify boundary retention and revision protection after deletion. Load one million representative IDs; measure storage.
actions.risk: Capacity exhaustion must reject without updating or acknowledging, never evict unexpired records.
